    4. Extensions

    Policies¶

    A policy extension packages a frozen policy so Eden can run it: a local actor (a checkpoint or an ONNX graph with its observation and action contract) or a client of a policy server (a VLA or world action model). Every policy is a PolicyBase subclass registered in POLICY_REGISTRY, run with eden inference --policy <name>. The policy zoo guide lists what each one needs, the remote policies guide explains server-backed clients, and extending policies shows how to add one.

    from eden.extensions.policies.base import POLICY_REGISTRY, PolicyBase
from eden.options.extensions.policies import PolicyOptions, RemotePolicyOptions

    Base class and registry¶

    Base classes for policy extensions.

    ClientMixin (server-backed policies) lives in :mod:eden.extensions.policies.client.

    Attributes¶

    POLICY_REGISTRY module-attribute ¶

    POLICY_REGISTRY = Registry('POLICY')

    Classes¶

    PolicyBase ¶

    PolicyBase(env: EnvBase, options: PolicyOptions)

    Bases: ConfigurableMixin[PolicyOptions]

    Base class for policies.

    Any object that takes observations and returns actions are defined as a policy.

    The *_options classmethods below describe the world the policy was trained in, and a task-less run (eden inference|deploy --policy) calls them for you. In :meth:action_options, :meth:observation_options and :meth:scene_entity_options, a parameter named after one of the policy's configurable attributes is filled from it (hand_name gets self.hand_name), so a name is declared once; entity_name is the caller's (--entity_name wins) and anything else keeps its own default. Parameters there therefore share a namespace with the class attributes — a knob that must keep its literal default needs a name no attribute uses. :meth:command_options is filled by the CLI instead (entity_name, motion_file, --clip_name), and :meth:robot_options / :meth:env_options take no arguments at all.

    :attr:reads_env_observations says which side of the env boundary the policy's step() sits on, and a deploy is arranged around the answer.

    Where a policy's files come from (registry, dataset, local_dir, assets_subdir) is fixed by the class, not configured per instance: a lookup that runs before any instance exists (a clip catalogue in :meth:command_options, a file an observation term loads) must read the same place __init__ does. To fetch from a mirror (an offline cluster, a shared read-only cache), set EDEN_ASSETS_DIR, or set local_dir on the class before anything reads it: MyPolicy.local_dir = "/data/mirror", as :meth:use_local_checkpoint redirects a checkpoint.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    checkpoint_path

    The path to the checkpoint file.
    Source code in eden/extensions/policies/base.py

    def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: PolicyOptions):
    super().__init__(options)
    self.env = env

    if self.checkpoint_path is not None:
        self.checkpoint_path = self.fetch_asset(self.checkpoint_path)
    self._verify_md5(self.checkpoint_path, self.md5_hash)

    Attributes¶

    reads_env_observations class-attribute instance-attribute ¶
    reads_env_observations: bool = False
    checkpoint_path class-attribute instance-attribute ¶
    checkpoint_path: str | None = None

    Methods:¶

    resolve_local_dir classmethod ¶

    @classmethod
def fetch_asset(cls, file: str) -> str:
    """The local path of ``file`` from this policy's Hub dataset, downloaded if missing.

    Fetches with the class's ``registry``, ``dataset`` and :meth:`resolve_local_dir`, so it gives the same
    path on the class (a lookup before any env exists) as on an instance. Call this rather than passing
    ``local_dir`` (``None`` by default) to ``get_asset_path`` yourself. Unlike ``EntityOptions.fetch_asset``,
    ``file`` is required: a policy has no single file of its own.
    """
    return get_asset_path(file, registry=cls.registry, dataset=cls.dataset, local_dir=cls.resolve_local_dir())

    Point a checkpoint at a local file and drop the hash pinned to the released one.

    The two go together: md5_hash pins the released weights, so setting the path without clearing it makes _verify_md5 reject the very file the caller asked for. Use this for every --ckpt-path-style flag rather than assigning the path by hand.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    path

    Local checkpoint to load instead of the released one. Not hashed: an unreleased file has no pinned digest to check it against.

    TYPE: str

    checkpoint_attr

    Which checkpoint to redirect, for policies that load more than one (sonic's decoder_checkpoint_path, omnixtreme's residual_/fk_). The hash attribute is derived from it by the naming convention every policy follows — <prefix>checkpoint_path is pinned by <prefix>md5_hash — and both are required to exist, so a policy that breaks the convention fails here rather than silently keeping a stale pin.

    @classmethod
def use_local_checkpoint(cls, path: str, *, checkpoint_attr: str = "checkpoint_path") -> None:
    """Point a checkpoint at a local file and drop the hash pinned to the released one.

    The two go together: ``md5_hash`` pins the *released* weights, so setting the path
    without clearing it makes ``_verify_md5`` reject the very file the caller asked
    for. Use this for every ``--ckpt-path``-style flag rather than assigning the path
    by hand.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path: str
        Local checkpoint to load instead of the released one. Not hashed: an
        unreleased file has no pinned digest to check it against.
    checkpoint_attr: str
        Which checkpoint to redirect, for policies that load more than one (sonic's
        ``decoder_checkpoint_path``, omnixtreme's ``residual_``/``fk_``). The hash
        attribute is derived from it by the naming convention every policy follows —
        ``<prefix>checkpoint_path`` is pinned by ``<prefix>md5_hash`` — and both are
        required to exist, so a policy that breaks the convention fails here rather
        than silently keeping a stale pin.
    """
    if not checkpoint_attr.endswith("checkpoint_path"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"checkpoint_attr must end with 'checkpoint_path' so its md5 attribute can be derived; "
            f"got {checkpoint_attr!r} on {cls.__name__}."
        )
    hash_attr = f"{checkpoint_attr.removesuffix('checkpoint_path')}md5_hash"
    for attr in (checkpoint_attr, hash_attr):
        if not hasattr(cls, attr):
            raise AttributeError(
                f"{cls.__name__} has no `{attr}`. `use_local_checkpoint` redirects "
                f"`{checkpoint_attr}` and clears `{hash_attr}` together; both must exist."
            )
    setattr(cls, checkpoint_attr, path)
    setattr(cls, hash_attr, None)

    def require_entity(self, name: str) -> Entity:
    """Resolve a scene entity the policy reads, failing loud when the scene has no such entity.

    Call this in ``__init__`` for every entity ``step()`` touches, so a scene missing one
    raises at construction rather than deep in the first step. In ``step()`` read
    ``self.env.entities[name]`` instead of caching the handle: deployment hot-swaps it.
    Resolves against the mapping, like a term's ``resolve_entity``.
    """
    return resolve_named_entity(
        self.env.entities,
        name,
        hint=(
            f"A task-less run builds the policy's own workspace from "
            f"{type(self).__name__}.scene_entity_options(); with --task, the task's scene "
            f"must declare '{name}'."
        ),
    )

    reset ¶
    reset(envs_idx: slice | Tensor | None = None) -> None

    Reset per-env policy state at episode boundaries.

    Override this in subclasses that hold per-env state across steps — e.g. heading offsets cached on the first step, last-action histories fed back as observations, attention KV caches, action-chunk queues. The default is a no-op, which is right for stateless policies.

    When used as a teacher / motion generator in long-horizon rollouts the owner is expected to call policy.reset(envs_idx) whenever the underlying env resets the corresponding envs.

    def __init__(self, **data):
    # Seed type metadata as construction data so BaseModel validates it into
    # __pydantic_extra__ (no-op for extra="forbid" classes, which use
    # the serialization envelope instead).
    data.update(option_metadata(self))
    # NOTE: all of the option modifications/validations should be done in the __init__ method
    try:
        BaseModel.__init__(self, **data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        # A misspelled field on an extra="forbid" class should teach the field set, not just
        # name the typo. Only rewritten when every error is extra_forbidden.
        enriched = _enrich_extra_forbidden(type(self), exc)
        if enriched is None:
            raise
        raise enriched from None

    Options for policy client extensions (ClientMixin).

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    host

    Policy server hostname, or a full URL (wss://example.com/ws, http://node:8000) whose scheme matches the transport.
    port

    Policy server port. None uses the port embedded in host (or the scheme's default when there is none); a port in host that disagrees with port raises.
    request_timeout

    Request timeout in seconds for HTTP transports.
    set_task_endpoint

    The server's set-task API (HTTP route); None (default) when the server has none and takes the task with each request.
    reset_endpoint

    The server's reset API: an HTTP route, a ZMQ endpoint name or a GalaxeaVLA reset message key; None (default) when the server has none, so a reset only clears local state.
    act_endpoint

    HTTP endpoint for requesting actions.
    task_description

    Language instruction sent on set_task / reset. Optional: policies without a language input leave it None.
    set_task_payload_key

    JSON key carrying the task description on set_task.
    reset_payload_key

    JSON key carrying the task description on reset.
    transport

    TRANSPORT_REGISTRY key selecting the wire protocol (http_json, http_json_numpy, http_multipart, openpi_websocket, galaxea_websocket, zmq_msgpack). Defaults to http_json.
    serializer

    SERIALIZER_REGISTRY key; None uses the transport's default.
    chunk_mode

    client (buffer the server's chunk and re-query when drained), server (the server caches the chunk and serves one row per call) or single (one action per call).
    pred_action_horizon

    Expected action-chunk length; None accepts any length.
    exec_horizon

    Rows executed open-loop before re-querying; None executes the whole chunk.
    short_chunk

    error raises when the server returns fewer than pred_action_horizon rows; accept queues what came back.
    chunk_temporal_ensemble_steps

    Temporal ensembling of the previous chunk's unused tail into the new head; zero keeps plain open-loop execution.
    chunk_temporal_ensemble_dims

    Restrict ensembling to the first N action dims (e.g. to spare a binary gripper).
    response_action_key

    Key holding the action chunk in a dict reply (action or actions).

    ONNX runtime helpers¶

    Shared ONNX-runtime infrastructure for policy extensions.

    Provides the session layer (provider selection, thread policy, CPU fallback) and a generic torch.nn.Module wrapper so policies don't each re-implement session creation + inference. Single-input / single-output graphs use :class:OnnxModule directly (see the sonic / holosoma ports); multi-input or IO-binding graphs subclass :class:_OnnxWrapperBase (see omnixtreme).

    def __init__(
    self,
    onnx_path: str,
    input_name: str,
    output_name: str,
    *,
    device: str | None = None,
    label: str = "ONNX",
    expected_input_dim: int | None = None,
    expected_output_dim: int | None = None,
    enable_iobinding: bool = False,
    dynamic_batch: bool = False,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(onnx_path, device=device, label=label, dynamic_batch=dynamic_batch)
    if input_name not in self._input_names:
        raise ValueError(f"{label} at {onnx_path} has no input '{input_name}'; got {sorted(self._input_names)}")
    if output_name not in self._output_names:
        raise ValueError(f"{label} at {onnx_path} has no output '{output_name}'; got {sorted(self._output_names)}")
    self._input_name = input_name
    self._output_name = output_name
    # Per-row (feature) element count, used by the swapped-graph guard. Works
    # whether the leading axis is a literal 1 or the symbolic "batch" that
    # dynamic_batch leaves behind.
    self.input_dim = _nonbatch_numel(self.session, input_name)
    self.output_dim = _nonbatch_numel(self.session, output_name)
    self._validate_dim("input", self.input_dim, expected_input_dim)
    self._validate_dim("output", self.output_dim, expected_output_dim)

    # Per-row output shape (dims after the dynamic batch axis), used to
    # pre-allocate the GPU output for IO-binding. None if any non-batch dim
    # is dynamic — then IO-binding is disabled and we use the numpy path.
    out = next((o for o in self.session.get_outputs() if o.name == output_name), None)
    out_shape = out.shape if out is not None else None
    tail = list(out_shape[1:]) if out_shape else []
    self._out_tail = tuple(int(d) for d in tail) if tail and all(isinstance(d, int) for d in tail) else None
    # IO-binding pre-allocates a float32 output buffer, so it's only sound
    # when the graph output is float32 (matching the numpy path, which casts
    # to float32). A non-float32 output (e.g. float16 / int) falls back to the
    # numpy path rather than writing wrong-width bytes into a float32 buffer.
    out_is_float32 = out is not None and out.type == "tensor(float)"
    self._iobind = bool(enable_iobinding) and self._out_tail is not None and out_is_float32

    output_dim instance-attribute ¶

    @torch.no_grad()
def forward(self, obs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    if self._iobind and self._can_iobind():
        try:
            return self._forward_iobind(obs)
        except Exception as e:
            if _env_bool("ONNX_DEBUG"):
                warnings.warn(f"[{self._label}] IO-binding failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); using numpy path")
    feed = {self._input_name: _ensure_2d(to_numpy(obs, np.float32))}
    return self._run(feed, output_names=[self._output_name])

    dynamic_batch_onnx ¶

    dynamic_batch_onnx(src: str) -> str

    Patch a static-batch-1 ONNX graph to accept an arbitrary leading batch.

    Rewrites every Reshape shape target whose leading dim is a constant 1 to -1 and marks each graph input/output's dim 0 as the symbolic "batch". The patched graph is cached next to src as *.dynbatch.onnx (falling back to a temp dir if src's directory is read-only) and the cached path is returned; an existing cache is reused.

    Needed because some released graphs (e.g. SONIC) are exported with a static batch of 1, which rejects num_envs > 1 feeds outright. The patch is a heuristic, so the freshly built graph is checked by :func:_verify_dynamic_batch (accepts a batched feed + permutation-equivariant rows) before it is used — a corrupt patch fails loudly here instead of silently returning wrong rows.

    def dynamic_batch_onnx(src: str) -> str:
    """Patch a static-batch-1 ONNX graph to accept an arbitrary leading batch.

    Rewrites every ``Reshape`` shape target whose leading dim is a constant ``1``
    to ``-1`` and marks each graph input/output's dim 0 as the symbolic
    ``"batch"``. The patched graph is cached next to ``src`` as
    ``*.dynbatch.onnx`` (falling back to a temp dir if ``src``'s directory is
    read-only) and the cached path is returned; an existing cache is reused.

    Needed because some released graphs (e.g. SONIC) are exported with a static
    batch of 1, which rejects ``num_envs > 1`` feeds outright. The patch is a
    heuristic, so the freshly built graph is checked by :func:`_verify_dynamic_batch`
    (accepts a batched feed + permutation-equivariant rows) before it is used — a
    corrupt patch fails loudly here instead of silently returning wrong rows.
    """
    # ``splitext`` (not ``str.replace``) so a path with ``.onnx`` in a parent dir
    # isn't corrupted, and an extensionless path can't collapse ``dst`` onto
    # ``src`` and overwrite the verified original.
    dst = os.path.splitext(src)[0] + ".dynbatch.onnx"

    # Reuse the cache only if it is at least as new as the source: a re-downloaded
    # / updated checkpoint at the same path (newer mtime) forces a rebuild, so we
    # never run a stale patch derived from older weights.
    def _cache_fresh(path: str) -> bool:
        return os.path.exists(path) and os.path.getmtime(path) >= os.path.getmtime(src)

    if _cache_fresh(dst):
        return dst
    import onnx
    from onnx import numpy_helper

    model = onnx.load(src)
    # Names of the shape tensors feeding every Reshape (constants + initializers).
    shape_inputs = {n.input[1] for n in model.graph.node if n.op_type == "Reshape"}

    def _lead_one_to_minus_one(t) -> bool:
        arr = numpy_helper.to_array(t).copy()
        # Only a leading literal 1 with no other inferred (-1) dim: a Reshape
        # target may carry at most one -1, so never introduce a second one
        # (transformer attention reshapes already use -1 for the flattened tail).
        if arr.ndim == 1 and arr.size and arr[0] == 1 and -1 not in arr.tolist():
            arr[0] = -1
            t.CopyFrom(numpy_helper.from_array(arr, t.name))
            return True
        return False

    for node in model.graph.node:
        if node.op_type == "Constant" and node.output[0] in shape_inputs:
            for attr in node.attribute:
                if attr.name == "value":
                    _lead_one_to_minus_one(attr.t)
    for init in model.graph.initializer:
        if init.name in shape_inputs:
            _lead_one_to_minus_one(init)
    for vi in list(model.graph.input) + list(model.graph.output):
        vi.type.tensor_type.shape.dim[0].dim_param = "batch"

    try:
        onnx.save(model, dst)
    except OSError:
        import hashlib
        import tempfile

        cache = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "eden_onnx_dynbatch")
        os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True)
        dst = os.path.join(cache, hashlib.md5(src.encode()).hexdigest() + ".dynbatch.onnx")
        if not _cache_fresh(dst):
            onnx.save(model, dst)
    # Just-built graph: confirm the patch is numerically equivalent to looped
    # batch-1 before any policy runs it. Cache hits above skip this (already
    # verified when first built).
    _verify_dynamic_batch(dst)
    return dst

    Server-backed clients¶

    A server-backed policy mixes in ClientMixin: it builds a request from the env's observations, sends it through a transport and serializer, and schedules the returned action chunk. The adapters turn a server's action format into the env's action terms.

    Server-backed policies: ClientMixin and the per-embodiment setup machinery.

    The counterpart of :mod:eden.extensions.policies.onnx (local actors): a client policy is class FooPolicy(ClientMixin, PolicyBase, ConfigurableMixin[RemotePolicyOptions]) whose inference happens on a server. The layer is policy-family neutral (VLA, world action model, remote RL controller, ...) and owns three things:

    • a transport from :mod:eden.utils.policy_client, selected by key (transport="http_json", "openpi_websocket", "zmq_msgpack", ...),
    • an :class:ActionChunkScheduler that turns server action chunks into one (num_envs, D) row per step,
    • a uniform lifecycle: :meth:ClientMixin.set_task, :meth:ClientMixin.reset_server, :meth:ClientMixin.reset.

    Every step runs the same pipeline::

    obs -> observe(obs)                                   per-step hooks (frame history, measured pose)
    -> [if scheduler.needs_inference]
          payload = pack_request(obs)                 default: pack_observations(obs)
          reply   = transport.infer(payload, request_options())
          chunk   = decode_response(reply)            -> (num_envs, T, D)
          scheduler.accept(chunk)
    -> row = scheduler.pop()                          -> (num_envs, D)
    -> unpack_actions(row)                            -> {action_term: tensor}

    step is also exposed as its stages observe (every step: frame histories, measured poses) / pack_request / infer_payload / accept_chunk / pop_action (plus :attr:ClientMixin.needs_inference). An evaluator can then run the blocking round-trip on a worker thread while it keeps stepping the simulation, so the robot moves on during the wait as much as the inference latency would let it. The evaluator must still call observe on every step. The contract is one request in flight: accept or discard its chunk before the next pack_request. Do not call reset / reset_server / set_task while a request is in flight, because nothing here locks or fences the transport.

    Servers that serve several embodiments use :class:SetupClientMixin with a SETUP_REGISTRY of :class:PolicySetupBase strategies selected by policy_setup.

    ActionChunkScheduler ¶

    ActionChunkScheduler(*, num_envs: int, mode: ChunkMode = 'client', pred_action_horizon: int | None = None, exec_horizon: int | None = None, short_chunk: ShortChunk = 'error', ensemble_steps: int = 0, ensemble_dims: int | None = None)

    Queue server action chunks and hand them out one row per env per step.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    num_envs

    Number of envs; chunks are (num_envs, T, D) and rows are (num_envs, D).

    TYPE: int

    mode

    client: this side owns the chunk and re-queries only when its queue drains. server: the server caches the chunk and serves one row per call, so every step is an inference call (GalaxeaVLA). single: the server returns one action per call (Octo). The latter two never buffer: a multi-row chunk raises.

    TYPE: ChunkMode DEFAULT: 'client'

    pred_action_horizon

    Expected chunk length T. None accepts any length.

    TYPE: int | None DEFAULT: None

    exec_horizon

    Rows executed before re-querying. None executes the whole chunk. Must not exceed pred_action_horizon when both are set.

    TYPE: int | None DEFAULT: None

    short_chunk

    What to do when the server returns fewer than pred_action_horizon rows: raise (the prediction is truncated relative to the trained horizon) or queue what came back.

    TYPE: ShortChunk DEFAULT: 'error'

    ensemble_steps

    Temporal ensembling of the previous chunk's unused tail into the new chunk's head: for K steps the old plan is weighted K/(K+1) … 1/(K+1). Zero disables it (bit-exact open-loop execution). Requires both horizons and ensemble_steps <= pred_action_horizon - exec_horizon.

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: 0

    ensemble_dims

    Only the first ensemble_dims action dims are ensembled (e.g. to keep a binary gripper channel untouched). None ensembles every dim.

    TYPE: int | None DEFAULT: None

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    num_envs: int,
    mode: ChunkMode = "client",
    pred_action_horizon: int | None = None,
    exec_horizon: int | None = None,
    short_chunk: ShortChunk = "error",
    ensemble_steps: int = 0,
    ensemble_dims: int | None = None,
) -> None:
    if mode not in ("client", "server", "single"):
        raise ValueError(f"chunk_mode must be 'client', 'server' or 'single', got {mode!r}")
    if short_chunk not in ("error", "accept"):
        raise ValueError(f"short_chunk must be 'error' or 'accept', got {short_chunk!r}")
    if pred_action_horizon is not None and pred_action_horizon <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"pred_action_horizon must be positive, got {pred_action_horizon}")
    if exec_horizon is not None and exec_horizon <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"exec_horizon must be positive, got {exec_horizon}")
    if pred_action_horizon is not None and exec_horizon is not None and exec_horizon > pred_action_horizon:
        raise ValueError(f"exec_horizon ({exec_horizon}) must be <= pred_action_horizon ({pred_action_horizon})")
    if ensemble_steps < 0:
        raise ValueError("chunk_temporal_ensemble_steps must be non-negative")
    if ensemble_steps > 0:
        if pred_action_horizon is None or exec_horizon is None:
            raise ValueError("temporal ensembling requires both pred_action_horizon and exec_horizon")
        available_overlap = pred_action_horizon - exec_horizon
        if ensemble_steps > available_overlap:
            raise ValueError(
                f"chunk_temporal_ensemble_steps ({ensemble_steps}) exceeds the unused "
                f"prediction tail ({available_overlap})"
            )
    if ensemble_dims is not None and ensemble_dims <= 0:
        raise ValueError("chunk_temporal_ensemble_dims must be positive or None")

    self.num_envs = int(num_envs)
    self.mode = mode
    self.pred_action_horizon = pred_action_horizon
    self.exec_horizon = exec_horizon
    self.short_chunk = short_chunk
    self.ensemble_steps = int(ensemble_steps)
    self.ensemble_dims = ensemble_dims

    self.queues: list[collections.deque[np.ndarray]] = [collections.deque() for _ in range(self.num_envs)]
    self.raw_queues: list[collections.deque[np.ndarray]] = [collections.deque() for _ in range(self.num_envs)]
    self._previous_unused_tail: list[np.ndarray | None] = [None] * self.num_envs
    self._last_take = 0
    # Diagnostics
    self.chunk_index = -1
    self.chunk_action_index = -1
    self.last_prediction_chunk_length = 0
    self.last_temporal_ensemble_steps = 0
    self.last_raw_row: np.ndarray | None = None

    def accept(self, chunk: np.ndarray, raw_chunk: np.ndarray | None = None) -> None:
    """Queue the first ``exec_horizon`` rows of a ``(num_envs, T, D)`` chunk.

    ``raw_chunk`` (same shape) is an optional untouched copy queued alongside for
    diagnostics, e.g. before a setup latched the gripper column.
    """
    chunk = np.asarray(chunk, dtype=np.float32)
    if chunk.ndim != 3 or chunk.shape[0] != self.num_envs:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected an action chunk of shape ({self.num_envs}, T, D), got {chunk.shape}")
    T = chunk.shape[1]
    if T == 0:
        raise ValueError("Policy server returned an empty action chunk.")
    if self.mode != "client" and T != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"chunk_mode={self.mode!r} expects one action per inference call, but the server returned "
            f"{T} rows. Use chunk_mode='client' if this server returns action chunks."
        )
    if raw_chunk is None:
        raw_chunk = chunk
    else:
        raw_chunk = np.asarray(raw_chunk, dtype=np.float32)
        if raw_chunk.shape != chunk.shape:
            raise ValueError(f"raw_chunk shape {raw_chunk.shape} does not match chunk shape {chunk.shape}")

    self.last_prediction_chunk_length = int(T)
    if self.pred_action_horizon is not None and T < self.pred_action_horizon and self.short_chunk == "error":
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Policy server returned {T} actions but pred_action_horizon={self.pred_action_horizon}. "
            "The prediction chunk is truncated — check the server's action_horizon before "
            "open-loop execution."
        )
    take = T if self.exec_horizon is None else min(self.exec_horizon, T)
    if self.pred_action_horizon is not None:
        take = min(take, self.pred_action_horizon)

    self.last_temporal_ensemble_steps = 0
    for i in range(self.num_envs):
        env_chunk = chunk[i]
        previous_tail = self._previous_unused_tail[i]
        if self.ensemble_steps > 0 and previous_tail is not None:
            overlap = min(self.ensemble_steps, previous_tail.shape[0], take)
            dims = env_chunk.shape[1] if self.ensemble_dims is None else min(self.ensemble_dims, env_chunk.shape[1])
            if overlap > 0:
                env_chunk = env_chunk.copy()
                # For K steps, old-plan weights are K/(K+1), ..., 1/(K+1): the new
                # observation-conditioned prediction takes over completely after K rows.
                old_weights = np.arange(overlap, 0, -1, dtype=np.float32) / float(self.ensemble_steps + 1)
                env_chunk[:overlap, :dims] = (
                    old_weights[:, None] * previous_tail[:overlap, :dims]
                    + (1.0 - old_weights[:, None]) * env_chunk[:overlap, :dims]
                )
                self.last_temporal_ensemble_steps = overlap
        self._previous_unused_tail[i] = chunk[i][take:].copy()
        self.queues[i].extend(env_chunk[:take])
        self.raw_queues[i].extend(raw_chunk[i][:take])

    self._last_take = int(take)
    self.chunk_index += 1

    def pop(self) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the next ``(num_envs, D)`` row; raises if nothing is queued."""
    if not self.queues[0]:
        raise RuntimeError("No queued action: call accept() with a server chunk before pop().")
    self.chunk_action_index = self._last_take - len(self.queues[0])
    rows = np.stack([q.popleft() for q in self.queues], axis=0)
    self.last_raw_row = np.stack([q.popleft() for q in self.raw_queues], axis=0)
    return rows

    FrameHistory ¶

    FrameHistory(horizon: int, stride: int)

    Per-step frame buffer that samples a strided temporal window the way delta_indices do.

    Servers trained with a video window (GR00T delta_indices=[-15, 0], RLDX-1 [-6, -4, -2, 0]) expect horizon frames spaced stride control steps apart, ending at the current one. :meth:append records one frame per control step and :meth:window returns (horizon, ...) in chronological order; missing history is padded with the oldest available frame, as the reference MultiStepWrapper does by seeding its deque with copies of the first observation.

    Built on :class:~eden.utils.buffers.circular_buffer.CircularBuffer (batch size 1, backfilled), so no per-key list bookkeeping is needed.

    def __init__(self, horizon: int, stride: int) -> None:
    if horizon < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"horizon must be >= 1, got {horizon}")
    if stride < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"stride must be >= 1, got {stride}")
    self.horizon = int(horizon)
    self.stride = int(stride)
    self._max_len = (self.horizon - 1) * self.stride + 1
    self._buffer: CircularBuffer | None = None

    def append(self, frame: np.ndarray | torch.Tensor) -> None:
    tensor = torch.as_tensor(frame)

    def window(self) -> np.ndarray:
    """``(horizon, ...)`` frames at ``stride`` spacing, newest last."""
    if self._buffer is None:
        raise RuntimeError("No frames recorded: call append() once per control step before window().")
    history = self._buffer.buffer[0]  # (max_len, ...) oldest -> newest, backfilled
    offsets = [(self.horizon - 1 - i) * self.stride for i in range(self.horizon)]
    return np.stack([history[self._max_len - 1 - off].cpu().numpy() for off in offsets], axis=0)

    ClientMixin ¶

    ClientMixin(env: EnvBase, options: PolicyOptions)

    Bases: ConfigurableMixin[ClientOptions]

    Mixin for policy extensions that delegate inference to a remote policy server.

    Concrete subclasses implement :meth:pack_observations and :meth:unpack_actions (the serialization contract between Eden's observation/action format and the server's API) and pick a transport. Everything else — connection handling, chunk queuing, horizon rules, task/reset lifecycle — is shared. Override :meth:decode_response when the reply does not carry the chunk under a single key, :meth:observe for per-step state the policy needs even on steps that do not query the server, and :meth:request_options for per-request server options (sessions, memory flags).

    Two requirements must both be met when combining with PolicyBase:

    1. ClientMixin must appear before PolicyBase so that its concrete :meth:step takes precedence over the abstract one.
    2. The subclass must re-parameterize ConfigurableMixin with the merged options type RemotePolicyOptions; otherwise __init_subclass__ inherits _options_class_ from whichever parent is first in MRO and :meth:configure rejects the other parent's fields.
    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    host

    Policy server address. host may be a full URL (wss://example.com/ws); use port=None to take the URL's port. See :func:eden.utils.policy_client.server_url.
    port

    Policy server address. host may be a full URL (wss://example.com/ws); use port=None to take the URL's port. See :func:eden.utils.policy_client.server_url.
    request_timeout

    Request timeout in seconds (HTTP transports).
    set_task_endpoint

    The server's set-task / reset API: an HTTP route, a ZMQ endpoint name or a GalaxeaVLA reset message key. None (the default) means the server has none, because it takes the task with each request, so :meth:set_task / :meth:reset_server only update local state. Declare one only when the official server exposes it.
    reset_endpoint

    The server's set-task / reset API: an HTTP route, a ZMQ endpoint name or a GalaxeaVLA reset message key. None (the default) means the server has none, because it takes the task with each request, so :meth:set_task / :meth:reset_server only update local state. Declare one only when the official server exposes it.
    act_endpoint

    HTTP route for inference.
    task_description

    Language instruction sent on set_task / reset; optional for policies with no language input.
    set_task_payload_key

    JSON keys carrying the task description.
    reset_payload_key

    JSON keys carrying the task description.
    transport

    TRANSPORT_REGISTRY key. Default "http_json".
    serializer

    SERIALIZER_REGISTRY key; None takes the transport's default.
    chunk_mode

    Who owns the action chunk: this client (buffer and re-query when drained), the server (it caches the chunk and serves one row per call), or nobody (one action per call).
    pred_action_horizon

    Expected chunk length from the server; None accepts any length.
    exec_horizon

    Rows executed open-loop before re-querying; None executes the whole chunk.
    short_chunk

    Whether a chunk shorter than pred_action_horizon is an error.

    def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: PolicyOptions):
    super().__init__(env, options)
    if not self.supports_batch and env.num_envs != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} has supports_batch=False and only supports "
            f"num_envs=1 (got {env.num_envs}). Set supports_batch=True on the "
            f"subclass if the remote server accepts batched requests."
        )
    if env.num_envs > 1 and type(self).reset is ClientMixin.reset:
        # The env resets its envs one by one; the default reset can only reset the shared
        # server state of all of them, so it would raise at the first episode end.
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} serves {env.num_envs} envs but keeps ClientMixin.reset, which "
            "refuses a partial reset because the server's episode state is shared by every env. Fix: "
            "override reset(envs_idx) with a per-env scheme (e.g. one server session per env), or "
            "run with num_envs=1."
        )
    self._num_envs: int = env.num_envs
    self._post_configure()
    self._scheduler = ActionChunkScheduler(
        num_envs=env.num_envs,
        mode=self.chunk_mode,
        pred_action_horizon=self.pred_action_horizon,
        exec_horizon=self.exec_horizon,
        short_chunk=self.short_chunk,
        ensemble_steps=self.chunk_temporal_ensemble_steps,
        ensemble_dims=self.chunk_temporal_ensemble_dims,
    )
    self.last_response_info: dict[str, Any] = {}
    self._transport: TransportBase = self.make_transport()
    self._post_connect()

    def transport_config(self) -> TransportConfig:
    """Collect the connection settings and the selected transport's knobs from this policy."""
    if self.transport not in TRANSPORT_REGISTRY.keys():
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__}.transport={self.transport!r} is not a registered transport. "
            f"Available: {sorted(TRANSPORT_REGISTRY.keys())}"
        )
    transport_cls = TRANSPORT_REGISTRY.get(self.transport)
    knobs = {name: getattr(self, name) for name in transport_cls.knobs if hasattr(self, name)}
    return TransportConfig(
        host=self.host,
        port=self.port,
        request_timeout=self.request_timeout,
        act_endpoint=self.act_endpoint,
        set_task_endpoint=self.set_task_endpoint,
        reset_endpoint=self.reset_endpoint,
        set_task_payload_key=self.set_task_payload_key,
        reset_payload_key=self.reset_payload_key,
        task_description=self.task_description,
        serializer=self.serializer,
        knobs=knobs,
    )

    PolicyBase hook: reset the server once every env this client serves is being reset.

    The server's episode state (history, chunk cache, recurrent memory) belongs to this client's connection / session as a whole, so a reset that covers every env maps to :meth:reset_server; with num_envs == 1 that is every non-empty reset. A partial reset of a batched client would wipe the other envs' state, so it raises until the client implements a per-env scheme (e.g. one server session per env).

    def reset(self, envs_idx: (slice | torch.Tensor) | None = None) -> None:
    """``PolicyBase`` hook: reset the server once every env this client serves is being reset.

    The server's episode state (history, chunk cache, recurrent memory) belongs to this
    client's connection / session as a whole, so a reset that covers every env maps to
    :meth:`reset_server`; with ``num_envs == 1`` that is every non-empty reset. A partial
    reset of a batched client would wipe the other envs' state, so it raises until the
    client implements a per-env scheme (e.g. one server session per env).
    """
    covered = self._reset_coverage(envs_idx)
    if covered == 0:
        return
    if covered < self.env.num_envs:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} cannot reset {covered} of {self.env.num_envs} envs: its server-side "
            "episode state is shared by all of them. Implement a per-env reset (e.g. one session per env)."
        )
    self.reset_server()

    def infer_payload(self, payload: Any) -> np.ndarray:
    """Blocking server round-trip -> ``(num_envs, T, D)`` chunk.

    Safe on a worker thread while the main thread keeps stepping the simulation, as long
    as it is the only call using the transport, i.e. no ``reset`` / ``reset_server`` /
    ``set_task`` until it returns.
    """
    response = self._transport.infer(payload, self.request_options())
    self._record_response_info(response)
    return self.decode_response(response)

    chunk = self._normalize_action_shape(np.asarray(chunk, dtype=np.float32))
    self._check_action_width(chunk, self.action_dim, schema=type(self).__name__)

    def step(self, obs: dict[str, torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    """Query the policy server when needed and return the next action in Eden format."""
    self.observe(obs)
    if self.needs_inference:
        self.accept_chunk(self.infer_payload(self.pack_request(obs)))
    return self.pop_action()

    def decode_response(self, response: Any) -> np.ndarray:
    """Extract the action chunk from a server reply as ``(num_envs, T, D)``.

    Default: ``response[response_action_key]`` normalized by
    :meth:`_normalize_action_shape`. Override for replies that spread the action over
    several keys.
    """
    if not isinstance(response, dict) or self.response_action_key not in response:
        raise KeyError(
            f"{type(self).__name__}: server reply has no {self.response_action_key!r} key "
            f"(got {sorted(response) if isinstance(response, dict) else type(response).__name__}). "
            "Set response_action_key or override decode_response()."
        )
    return self._normalize_action_shape(np.asarray(response[self.response_action_key], dtype=np.float32))

    PolicySetupBase ¶

    PolicySetupBase(policy: SetupClientMixin)

    Bases: ABC

    Strategy object for one server embodiment / schema.

    Class-level defaults (pred_action_horizon, exec_horizon, default_image_size) fill the policy's pred_action_horizon / exec_horizon / image_size when the policy leaves them None, so each setup can carry the horizon and resolution its checkpoint was trained with.

    Concrete setups own observation_options / action_options (classmethod factories so the env can be built without a live policy), pack_observations, and unpack_actions; they optionally override decode_response (reply -> (T, D) chunk), observe (per-step state) and reset.

    def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: PolicyOptions):
    super().__init__(env, options)
    if not self.supports_batch and env.num_envs != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} has supports_batch=False and only supports "
            f"num_envs=1 (got {env.num_envs}). Set supports_batch=True on the "
            f"subclass if the remote server accepts batched requests."
        )
    if env.num_envs > 1 and type(self).reset is ClientMixin.reset:
        # The env resets its envs one by one; the default reset can only reset the shared
        # server state of all of them, so it would raise at the first episode end.
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} serves {env.num_envs} envs but keeps ClientMixin.reset, which "
            "refuses a partial reset because the server's episode state is shared by every env. Fix: "
            "override reset(envs_idx) with a per-env scheme (e.g. one server session per env), or "
            "run with num_envs=1."
        )
    self._num_envs: int = env.num_envs
    self._post_configure()
    self._scheduler = ActionChunkScheduler(
        num_envs=env.num_envs,
        mode=self.chunk_mode,
        pred_action_horizon=self.pred_action_horizon,
        exec_horizon=self.exec_horizon,
        short_chunk=self.short_chunk,
        ensemble_steps=self.chunk_temporal_ensemble_steps,
        ensemble_dims=self.chunk_temporal_ensemble_dims,
    )
    self.last_response_info: dict[str, Any] = {}
    self._transport: TransportBase = self.make_transport()
    self._post_connect()

    def accept_chunk(self, chunk: np.ndarray) -> None:
    chunk = self._normalize_action_shape(np.asarray(chunk, dtype=np.float32))
    self._check_action_width(
        chunk, type(self._setup).action_dim, schema=f"{type(self).__name__} setup {self.policy_setup!r}"
    )
    raw, self._setup.last_raw_action_chunk = self._setup.last_raw_action_chunk, None
    raw_chunk = None if raw is None else self._normalize_action_shape(np.asarray(raw, dtype=np.float32))
    self._scheduler.accept(chunk, raw_chunk=raw_chunk)

    def unpack_actions(self, raw_action: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    raw_action = np.asarray(raw_action)
    if raw_action.ndim == 2:
        if raw_action.shape[0] != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} setups decode one env at a time; got a batched row {raw_action.shape}."
            )
        raw_action = raw_action[0]
    return self._setup.unpack_actions(raw_action)

    def concat_action_streams(action_dict: dict[str, np.ndarray], keys: tuple[str, ...]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Concatenate per-key ``(1, T, d_k)`` action streams in ``keys`` order into one ``(T, D)`` chunk.

    Servers of the Isaac-GR00T family answer with one array per modality key. A ``(T, d)``
    array (batch already squeezed) is accepted; a batch larger than one is rejected because
    the client serves a single env.
    """
    cols = []
    for key in keys:
        if key not in action_dict:
            raise KeyError(f"Server reply lacks action key {key!r}; got {sorted(action_dict)}")
        arr = np.asarray(action_dict[key], dtype=np.float32)
        if arr.ndim == 2:  # (T, d) — server already squeezed the batch axis
            arr = arr[np.newaxis]
        if arr.ndim != 3:
            raise ValueError(f"Action key {key!r} must be (B, T, d); got shape {arr.shape}")
        if arr.shape[0] != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"Remote clients serve num_envs=1; action key {key!r} has batch={arr.shape[0]}")
        cols.append(arr[0])  # (T, d)
    return np.concatenate(cols, axis=-1).astype(np.float32)

    def validate_modality_config(config: dict, schema: ModalitySchema, *, setup_name: str) -> None:
    """Raise ``ValueError`` when ``config`` (a ``get_modality_config`` reply) contradicts ``schema``.

    An empty ``config`` means the server advertises nothing and passes. Keys are compared
    as sets for video / state (payloads are keyed dicts) and as an ordered list for action
    (the client concatenates streams in that order); horizons come from ``delta_indices``.
    """
    if not config:
        return
    problems: list[str] = []

    def modality(name: str) -> dict | None:
        entry = config.get(name)
        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "modality_keys" not in entry:
            problems.append(f"server config has no {name!r} modality with modality_keys (got {sorted(config)})")
            return None
        return entry

    video, state, action, language = (modality(k) for k in ("video", "state", "action", "language"))
    if video is not None:
        served = tuple(video["modality_keys"])
        if set(served) != set(schema.video_keys):
            problems.append(f"video keys: setup packs {sorted(schema.video_keys)}, server serves {sorted(served)}")
        delta = list(video.get("delta_indices", []))
        if delta and len(delta) != schema.video_horizon:
            problems.append(
                f"video horizon: setup sends {schema.video_horizon} frame(s), server expects {len(delta)} ({delta})"
            )
        elif len(delta) > 1:
            strides = {b - a for a, b in zip(delta[:-1], delta[1:])}
            if strides != {schema.video_stride}:
                problems.append(
                    f"video stride: setup samples every {schema.video_stride} step(s), server expects {delta}"
                )
    if state is not None:
        served = tuple(state["modality_keys"])
        if set(served) != set(schema.state_keys):
            problems.append(f"state keys: setup packs {sorted(schema.state_keys)}, server serves {sorted(served)}")
    if action is not None:
        served = tuple(action["modality_keys"])
        if served != tuple(schema.action_keys):
            problems.append(
                f"action keys (order matters): setup decodes {list(schema.action_keys)}, server serves {list(served)}"
            )
        delta = list(action.get("delta_indices", []))
        if schema.action_horizon is not None and delta and len(delta) != schema.action_horizon:
            problems.append(f"action horizon: setup expects {schema.action_horizon} rows, server predicts {len(delta)}")
    if language is not None and schema.language_key not in tuple(language["modality_keys"]):
        problems.append(
            f"language key: setup sends {schema.language_key!r}, server accepts {list(language['modality_keys'])}"
        )

    if problems:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Setup {setup_name!r} does not match the served checkpoint's modality config:\n  - "
            + "\n  - ".join(problems)
        )

    Action adapters¶

    Manipulation action adapters for remote policy clients.

    An adapter converts a raw action array returned by a policy server into the {controller_name: torch.Tensor} dict that Eden's action manager expects. It is the mirror image of the server-specific obs packer: the packer serializes Eden's world state for the server; the adapter deserializes the server's action chunk back into Eden's controller contract.

    The adapters here are transport-agnostic on purpose — they are composed into per-setup strategies (OpenPI pi/, GR00T, RLDX-1, Cosmos3, GalaxeaVLA) but nothing about them is wire-specific, so any client policy that receives a numpy action vector can reuse them. They are the manipulation family's decoders; other families add their own module beside this one. The module also carries the manipulation-side composition helpers shared by the setups (image observation groups, the WidowX EE-delta action pair, robot DOF layouts read from the robot option classes) and the construction checks every client runs against the env it is given (check_*: the control rate, the gripper decision term, the plain proprio group, joint terms that pass commands through, the DROID arm term and joint state, LIBERO's camera resolution).

    Four adapter shapes cover the setups that use them:

    • :class:EEDeltaAdapter — 7-D [ee_delta(6), gripper(1)] for the WidowX/Bridge and Google-Robot setups (OpenPI, GR00T, Octo). Euler or axis-angle rotation deltas; both reach the IK controller as a rotation vector.
    • :class:JointVelocityAdapter — (n_arm + 1)-D joint velocity + gripper for OpenPI DROID. Emits true velocity commands by default, with an optional position-integration fallback for arms without a usable velocity controller.
    • :class:JointPositionAdapter — (n_arm + 1)-D absolute joint position targets + gripper for DROID joint-position checkpoints (OpenPI, Cosmos3, GalaxeaVLA).
    • :class:BimanualJointPositionAdapter — 14-D joint positions split into two arm controllers for Aloha.

    None of them decides the gripper: each forwards the server's gripper scalar to the env's GripperDecisionController, which applies the setup's rule (threshold, hysteresis, sticky latch). See :func:check_env_gripper_term.

    Output dict: * ee_controller — (num_envs, 6) [dxyz, rotation vector]: the task-space delta :class:DifferentialIKController solves J @ dq = delta for, whose angular rows are an angular displacement (axis * angle), not Euler angles. * gripper_controller — (num_envs, 1) the server's gripper scalar, unchanged; the env's GripperDecisionController interprets it (openness / sign / sticky latch, per setup).

    JointVelocityAdapter ¶

    JointVelocityAdapter(*, n_arm: int = 7, entity_name: str = 'robot', arm_dofs_name: list[str] | None = None, dt: float | None = None, mode: Literal['velocity', 'velocity_integrate'] = 'velocity', action_scale: float | list[float] = 1.0, clip: float = 1.0, velocity_lag: dict[str, 'Sequence[float]'] | None = None, velocity_compensation: dict[str, 'Sequence[float]'] | None = None, velocity_lag_dt: float | None = None, gripper_threshold: float = 0.5, debug_gripper: bool = False, arm_key: str = 'ee_controller', gripper_key: str = 'gripper_controller')

    Bases: _JointAdapterBase

    Adapter for joint-velocity + gripper actions (DROID).

    Pi0 DROID returns (T, 8) chunks where the first 7 dims are joint velocities in DROID's unit action space, not rad/s, and the last dim is a gripper command binarized at 0.5 on the robot side (here by the env's GripperDecisionController). openpi's examples/droid/main.py clips every dim element-wise to [-1, 1] before RobotEnv.step (which leaves DROID's own v / max|v| rescale nothing to do), and DROID's RobotIKSolver.joint_velocity_to_delta turns a unit velocity into max_joint_delta = 0.2 rad per 15 Hz control step, i.e. 3 rad/s per unit. That conversion is the caller's action_scale (DroidSetup passes 3.0 with clip=1.0 and dt=1/15 s); the default action_scale=1.0 is a pass-through and is not DROID's.

    In mode="velocity" (default), the arm output is action_scale * clip(v), the rad/s velocity command consumed by :class:ImplicitVelocityController.

    In mode="velocity_integrate", this adapter integrates velocities to joint-position targets on the client side::

    target_pos = current_pos + dt * action_scale * clip(v, -1, 1)

    and the integrated target is consumed by a standard :class:ImplicitPDController.

    Limitation: client-side integration assumes the downstream position controller tracks the reference cleanly. Stiff Franka-like gains usually do, but over long horizons small integration errors accumulate; prefer mode="velocity" wherever the arm has an ImplicitVelocityController.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    n_arm

    Number of arm joints (length of the velocity slice in raw_action).

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: 7

    entity_name

    Eden entity name used to read current joint positions for integration.

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: 'robot'

    arm_dofs_name

    Ordered DOF names under entity_name, one per arm joint. Must match the dofs_name list on the downstream arm controller. Required by the integration modes (resolved on the env in :meth:bind); unused in mode="velocity".

    TYPE: list[str] | None DEFAULT: None

    dt

    Integration timestep (seconds). If None, uses env.dt. Only used by integration modes.

    TYPE: float | None DEFAULT: None

    mode

    velocity emits rad/s commands directly. velocity_integrate integrates them into position targets (the fallback above).

    TYPE: ('velocity', 'velocity_integrate') DEFAULT: "velocity"

    action_scale

    Rad/s per unit of the clipped arm output, applied before it is sent to the downstream controller (scalar, or one value per arm joint). DROID's is 3.0: 0.2 rad per 1/15 s control step (DROID_RAD_PER_S_PER_UNIT in the pi setups). The default 1.0 passes the clipped value through, which is right only for a server whose arm output is already rad/s.

    TYPE: float | list[float] DEFAULT: 1.0

    clip

    Each arm dim is clipped element-wise to [-clip, clip] before scaling, in the server's units (DROID: openpi's [-1, 1] unit-space clip, so at most 3 rad/s per joint after the 3.0 scale).

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

    velocity_lag

    Optional {"tau_s": (n_arm,), "dc_gain": (n_arm,)} first-order lag applied to the commanded velocity in mode="velocity", modelling the real robot's controller bandwidth (Genesis's velocity actuator is ~10x faster than DROID's). None (default) is an exact no-op. See :class:_FirstOrderLag.

    TYPE: dict | None DEFAULT: None

    velocity_compensation

    Optional {"real_tau_s", "real_dc_gain", "sim_tau_s", "sim_dc_gain"} (each (n_arm,)): the H_real / H_sim command filter, in mode="velocity". Mutually exclusive with velocity_lag.

    TYPE: dict | None DEFAULT: None

    velocity_lag_dt

    The period between two adapter calls in seconds, required when velocity_lag or velocity_compensation is set. A :class:~eden.extensions.policies.client.ClientMixin client executes one action row per env step, so for it this is env.dt (DroidSetup pins that to DROID's 1/15 s and passes it). Only an evaluator that holds one action across several env steps has a longer one (e.g. 0.064 s on a 20 ms env), which is why it is passed rather than read from the env.

    TYPE: float | None DEFAULT: None

    gripper_threshold

    Closedness above which the diagnostics label the gripper intent "close". The scalar itself is forwarded unchanged; the env's GripperDecisionController decides.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.5

    debug_gripper

    Log each gripper scalar and its intent.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    arm_key

    Keys in the returned dict — must match the controller names registered in the env's action manager.

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: 'ee_controller'

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    n_arm: int = 7,
    entity_name: str = "robot",
    arm_dofs_name: list[str] | None = None,
    dt: float | None = None,
    mode: Literal["velocity", "velocity_integrate"] = "velocity",
    action_scale: float | list[float] = 1.0,
    clip: float = 1.0,
    velocity_lag: dict[str, "Sequence[float]"] | None = None,
    velocity_compensation: dict[str, "Sequence[float]"] | None = None,
    velocity_lag_dt: float | None = None,
    gripper_threshold: float = 0.5,
    debug_gripper: bool = False,
    arm_key: str = "ee_controller",
    gripper_key: str = "gripper_controller",
):
    super().__init__(
        n_arm=n_arm,
        gripper_threshold=gripper_threshold,
        debug_gripper=debug_gripper,
        arm_key=arm_key,
        gripper_key=gripper_key,
    )
    if mode not in ("velocity", "velocity_integrate"):
        raise ValueError(f"JointVelocityAdapter.mode must be 'velocity' or 'velocity_integrate', got {mode!r}")
    self.mode = mode
    self.entity_name = entity_name
    self.arm_dofs_name = None if arm_dofs_name is None else list(arm_dofs_name)
    if mode != "velocity":
        if self.arm_dofs_name is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"JointVelocityAdapter(mode={mode!r}) integrates from the arm's current joint positions, so "
                f"it needs arm_dofs_name: the {n_arm} arm joint names on {entity_name!r}, in the arm "
                "controller's dofs_name order."
            )
        if len(self.arm_dofs_name) != n_arm:
            raise ValueError(
                f"JointVelocityAdapter: arm_dofs_name names {len(self.arm_dofs_name)} joints "
                f"({self.arm_dofs_name}), but n_arm={n_arm}. Fix: pass exactly one name per arm joint."
            )
    if dt is not None and (not np.isfinite(dt) or dt <= 0.0):
        raise ValueError(f"dt must be a positive finite action period, got {dt!r}")
    self.dt = None if dt is None else float(dt)

    # Shape () or (n_arm,): broadcasts over the arm velocities either way.
    self.action_scale = np.array(action_scale, dtype=np.float32)
    if self.action_scale.shape not in ((), (n_arm,)):
        raise ValueError(
            "action_scale must be a scalar or have one value per arm joint; "
            f"expected shape ({n_arm},), got {self.action_scale.shape}"
        )
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(self.action_scale)):
        raise ValueError("action_scale must contain only finite values")
    if not np.isfinite(clip) or clip <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"clip must be positive and finite, got {clip!r}")
    self.clip = float(clip)

    self._velocity_filter = self._make_velocity_filter(velocity_lag, velocity_compensation, velocity_lag_dt)
    self.velocity_lag_dt = None if velocity_lag_dt is None else float(velocity_lag_dt)
    self._arm_dofs_idx_local: torch.Tensor | None = None

    def bind(self, env: "EnvBase") -> None:
    """Resolve the arm joints the integration modes read, once, against ``env``.

    Only the derived indices are cached; the entity is looked up on every call, since
    deployment can swap ``env.entities[entity_name]``.
    """
    if self.mode == "velocity":
        return
    if self.entity_name not in env.entities:
        raise ValueError(
            f"JointVelocityAdapter.entity_name={self.entity_name!r} is not an entity of the env. "
            f"Available: {sorted(env.entities)}"
        )
    selection = env.entities[self.entity_name].find_named_dofs(self.arm_dofs_name)
    if len(selection.names) != self.n_arm:
        raise ValueError(
            f"JointVelocityAdapter: arm_dofs_name {self.arm_dofs_name} selects {len(selection.names)} joints "
            f"on {self.entity_name!r} ({list(selection.names)}), but n_arm={self.n_arm}. Fix: name each arm "
            "joint exactly (a glob can match more joints than intended)."

    Adapter for absolute joint-position + gripper actions.

    ee_delta_to_world(delta_b: Tensor, base_quat_w: Tensor) -> Tensor

    A robot-base-frame (num_envs, 6) [dxyz, rotation vector] delta in the world frame.

    EE-delta servers (Bridge, Fractal, RobotArena) compose their deltas in the robot base frame, while :class:DifferentialIKController solves against the world-frame Jacobian: the two agree only for a base with identity rotation. Both parts are displacements, so the base's world orientation base_quat_w ((num_envs, 4) wxyz, the controlled entity's get_quat()) alone maps them.

    def ee_delta_to_world(delta_b: torch.Tensor, base_quat_w: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """A robot-base-frame ``(num_envs, 6)`` ``[dxyz, rotation vector]`` delta in the world frame.

    EE-delta servers (Bridge, Fractal, RobotArena) compose their deltas in the robot base frame, while
    :class:`DifferentialIKController` solves against the world-frame Jacobian: the two agree only for a
    base with identity rotation. Both parts are displacements, so the base's world orientation
    ``base_quat_w`` (``(num_envs, 4)`` wxyz, the controlled entity's ``get_quat()``) alone maps them.
    """
    return torch.cat(
        [transform_by_quat(delta_b[:, :3], base_quat_w), transform_by_quat(delta_b[:, 3:6], base_quat_w)], dim=-1
    )

    def bridge_rpy(quat_wxyz: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Bridge / SimplerEnv WidowX ``rpy``: the EE rotation relative to :data:`BRIDGE_DEFAULT_ROT`, xyz Euler.

    ``R @ BRIDGE_DEFAULT_ROT.T`` as quaternions, decomposed into extrinsic xyz Euler angles.
    """
    quat = torch.as_tensor(quat_wxyz, dtype=torch.float64)
    return torch.stack(euler_xyz_from_quat(quat_mul(quat, _BRIDGE_DEFAULT_QUAT_INV))).numpy()

    Robosuite's quat2axisangle for a wxyz quaternion, as LIBERO's official clients compute EE state.

    Both OpenPI (examples/libero/main.py) and Isaac-GR00T (gr00t/eval/sim/LIBERO/libero_env.py) copy it. Kept robosuite-exact -- no sign canonicalisation (the angle may exceed pi when w < 0), hard zero at the singularity -- rather than routed through :func:eden.utils.geom.axis_angle_from_quat or Rotation.as_rotvec, because the servers' normalisation statistics were fit on robosuite's output.

    def robosuite_axis_angle(quat_wxyz: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Robosuite's ``quat2axisangle`` for a wxyz quaternion, as LIBERO's official clients compute EE state.

    Both OpenPI (``examples/libero/main.py``) and Isaac-GR00T (``gr00t/eval/sim/LIBERO/libero_env.py``)
    copy it. Kept robosuite-exact -- no sign canonicalisation (the angle may exceed pi when w < 0), hard
    zero at the singularity -- rather than routed through :func:`eden.utils.geom.axis_angle_from_quat` or
    ``Rotation.as_rotvec``, because the servers' normalisation statistics were fit on robosuite's output.
    """
    w, x, y, z = quat_wxyz
    w = float(np.clip(w, -1.0, 1.0))
    den = math.sqrt(max(0.0, 1.0 - w * w))
    if math.isclose(den, 0.0):
        return np.zeros(3)
    angle = 2.0 * math.acos(w)
    return np.array([x, y, z]) * angle / den

    def libero_task_action_options() -> dict[str, "ActionTermOptions"]:
    """The stock ``libero`` task's action terms, from the task's own builder (no restated constants).

    ``osc_pose`` (robosuite ``OSC_POSE`` on the grip site) and ``gripper`` (the stateful
    ``LiberoPandaGripperController``, ``+1`` closes / ``-1`` opens): the controllers LIBERO's
    demonstrations, and so every LIBERO checkpoint (OpenPI, GR00T), were recorded with.
    """
    from eden.tasks.libero.config import _make_action_options

    options = _make_action_options()
    # term_keys(), not model_extra: the extras also carry the _option_module_ / _option_class_ markers.
    return {name: getattr(options, name) for name in options.term_keys()}

    def check_libero_camera_resolution(env, *, subject: str, trained_on: str, wrong_fix: str) -> None:
    """Refuse an env whose ``image`` / ``wrist_image`` groups render at another size than LIBERO's 256x256.

    The camera is the one each group's term names in ``params["camera_name"]`` (:func:`make_image_groups`);
    a camera term without one is judged by the image its group publishes. ``subject`` names the client and
    setup, ``trained_on`` the upstream render the checkpoints saw, and ``wrong_fix`` is the closing "Do not
    ..." sentence about the client's own image-size knob. Envs without an observation manager skip.
    """
    manager = getattr(env, "observation_manager", None)
    if manager is None:
        return
    width, height = LIBERO_CAMERA_RESOLUTION
    for group, name, term in manager.iter_terms():
        if group not in ("image", "wrist_image"):
            continue
        camera = (getattr(term, "params", None) or {}).get("camera_name")
        if camera is None:
            rows, cols = manager.group_obs_dim[group][:2]
            resolution, where, camera = (
                (int(cols), int(rows)),
                f"the camera behind observation term {group}/{name}",
                "<camera>",
            )
        else:
            resolution = tuple(int(v) for v in env.cameras[camera].cam_resolution)
            where = f"camera {camera!r} (observation term {group}/{name})"
        if resolution == LIBERO_CAMERA_RESOLUTION:
            continue
        raise ValueError(
            f"{subject} sends {where}, which renders at cam_resolution={resolution}, but {trained_on}, so the frame "
            f"would be upsampled off that distribution. Fix: in the env's cameras_options set the {camera!r} camera's "
            f"cam_resolution=({width}, {height}), e.g. cfg.cameras_options.{camera}.cam_resolution = ({width}, "
            f"{height}). {wrong_fix}"
        )

    def libero_training_view(image: torch.Tensor | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """An upright Eden render as LIBERO's training images show it: mirrored left-right, ``(H, W, 3)`` uint8.

    LIBERO's official clients send ``obs["agentview_image"][::-1, ::-1]`` and the same for
    ``robot0_eye_in_hand_image`` (OpenPI ``examples/libero/main.py`` lines 115-116, Isaac-GR00T
    ``gr00t/eval/sim/LIBERO/libero_env.py`` lines 148-149), as the LIBERO datasets were recorded. robosuite
    1.4's raw frame is OpenGL bottom-up (the upright view flipped vertically), so that pair of flips leaves the
    upright view mirrored left-right. Eden renders upright, so only the left-right mirror reproduces it;
    porting ``[::-1, ::-1]`` literally would turn the image upside down.
    """
    return np.ascontiguousarray(to_uint8_hwc(image)[:, ::-1])

    def dofs_pos_joint_names(env: "EnvBase", term) -> list[str]:
    """The joints a built ``DofsPos`` term reads, in its column order."""
    entity = env.entities[term.entity_name]
    if term.dofs_name is not None:
        return list(entity.find_named_dofs(list(term.dofs_name)).names)
    if term.terms_idx is not None:
        return [entity.dofs_name[idx] for idx in term.terms_idx]
    return list(entity.dofs_name)

    def make_image_groups(
    camera_name: str,
    use_wrist_image: bool,
    wrist_camera_name: str,
) -> dict[str, ObservationGroupOptions]:
    """Build ``image`` (and optionally ``wrist_image``) observation groups, one ``rgb`` term each."""
    from eden.managers.terms.observations.camera import rgb_image
    from eden.options.managers.observations import ObservationGroupOptions
    from eden.terms import ObsTerm

    groups: dict[str, ObservationGroupOptions] = {
        "image": ObservationGroupOptions(
            rgb=ObsTerm.configure(func=rgb_image, params={"camera_name": camera_name}),
        ),
    }
    if use_wrist_image:
        groups["wrist_image"] = ObservationGroupOptions(
            rgb=ObsTerm.configure(func=rgb_image, params={"camera_name": wrist_camera_name}),
        )
    return groups

    def make_ee_pose_group(
    entity_name: str,
    ee_link_name: str,
    *,
    gripper_entity_name: str | None,
    gripper_dof_name: str,
    open_gripper_pos: float = WidowX250.open_finger_pos,
    gripper_close_pos: float = ROBOTIQ_CLOSE_POS,
    offset_pos: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
) -> ObservationGroupOptions:
    """``[ee_pos(3), ee_quat_wxyz(4), gripper_openness(1)]`` proprio group (Bridge / Google-robot / RobotArena).

    With the gripper on the arm entity, openness is ``pos / open_gripper_pos`` (WidowX fingers:
    fully open at ``open_gripper_pos``, closed at 0). With a separately mounted gripper it is
    ``1 - pos / gripper_close_pos`` (Robotiq driver: open at 0, closed at ``gripper_close_pos``).
    """
    from eden.managers.terms.observations.manipulation import EndEffectorPose, GripperState
    from eden.options.managers.observations import ObservationGroupOptions

    if gripper_entity_name is None:  # WidowX fingers on the arm: open at open_gripper_pos, closed at 0
        gripper_entity_name, open_pos, close_pos = entity_name, open_gripper_pos, 0.0
    else:  # a mounted Robotiq: open at 0, closed at gripper_close_pos
        open_pos, close_pos = 0.0, gripper_close_pos
    return ObservationGroupOptions(
        ee_pose=EndEffectorPose.configure(
            entity_name=entity_name, ee_link_name=ee_link_name, rotation="quat", offset_pos=tuple(offset_pos)
        ),
        gripper=GripperState.configure(
            entity_name=gripper_entity_name,
            dofs_name=[gripper_dof_name],
            normalize="openness",
            open_pos=open_pos,
            close_pos=close_pos,
        ),
    )

    def make_widowx_ee_delta_actions(
    entity_name: str,
    ee_link_name: str,
    dofs_name: list[str],
    scale: float,
    *,
    gripper_input: str = "openness",
    gripper_threshold: float = 0.5,
    gripper_sticky_repeats: int = 0,
    gripper_zero_holds: bool = False,
) -> dict[str, ActionTermOptions]:
    """``ee_controller`` (differential IK) + ``gripper_controller`` for WidowX EE-delta policies.

    The gripper term is a :class:`~eden.managers.terms.actions.binary_actions.GripperDecisionController`
    that receives the server's raw gripper scalar (Bridge servers emit *openness*, ``> 0.5`` =
    open) and decides open/close itself; ``gripper_sticky_repeats`` enables the fractal latch
    the Google-robot checkpoints were trained with.
    """
    from eden.managers.terms.actions.binary_actions import GripperDecisionController
    from eden.managers.terms.actions.task_space_actions import DifferentialIKController

    return dict(
        ee_controller=DifferentialIKController.configure(
            entity_name=entity_name,
            ee_link_name=ee_link_name,
            dofs_name=dofs_name,
            position_scale=scale,
            orientation_scale=scale,
        ),
        gripper_controller=GripperDecisionController.configure(
            entity_name=entity_name,
            dofs_name=list(WidowX250.gripper_dofs_name),
            open_action={"left_finger": WidowX250.open_finger_pos, "right_finger": -WidowX250.open_finger_pos},
            close_action=0.0,
            input=gripper_input,
            threshold=gripper_threshold,
            sticky_repeats=gripper_sticky_repeats,
            zero_holds=gripper_zero_holds,
        ),
    )

    def make_droid_joint_position_actions(
    arm_entity_name: str = "robot",
    arm_dofs_name: list[str] | None = None,
    *,
    gripper_entity_name: str | None = None,
    gripper_dof_name: str = "left_driver_joint",
    arm_key: str = "ee_controller",
    **gripper_options,
) -> dict[str, ActionTermOptions]:
    """Absolute DROID arm joint targets + the Robotiq gripper term, as joint-position DROID servers need.

    The servers return absolute joint targets, so the arm is an ``ImplicitPDController`` with a zero
    reference. The gripper is :func:`make_droid_gripper_action` on ``gripper_entity_name`` (the arm
    entity when the Robotiq is part of it), configured by ``gripper_options``.
    """
    from eden.constants import ReferenceSource
    from eden.managers.terms.actions.joint_actions import ImplicitPDController

    arm = ImplicitPDController.configure(
        entity_name=arm_entity_name,
        dofs_name=list(DROID_ARM_DOFS) if arm_dofs_name is None else list(arm_dofs_name),
        reference_source=ReferenceSource.ZERO,
    )
    gripper = make_droid_gripper_action(
        gripper_entity_name if gripper_entity_name is not None else arm_entity_name,
        gripper_dof_name,
        **gripper_options,
    )
    return {arm_key: arm, "gripper_controller": gripper}

    Refuse an env whose control period env.dt is not the upstream client's 1 / control_hz s.

    A remote checkpoint's rows are one upstream control step each (an EE or joint delta, the next waypoint of a trajectory), and exec_horizon / a video window's stride count env steps, so at another rate every chunk executes at the wrong speed, silently. subject names the client and setup ("PiPolicy.policy_setup='droid'") and source where upstream sets the rate. timing is the (sim_dt as typed, decimation) the fix suggests, with timing_note appended (e.g. the sim_substeps a Robotiq 2F85 needs); None derives one from the env's sim_dt. wrong_fix replaces the closing "do not rescale or resample the actions" sentence for a client with a more plausible wrong fix.

    def check_control_rate(
    env: "EnvBase",
    *,
    control_hz: float,
    subject: str,
    source: str,
    timing: tuple[str, int] | None = None,
    timing_note: str = "",
    wrong_fix: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Refuse an env whose control period ``env.dt`` is not the upstream client's ``1 / control_hz`` s.

    A remote checkpoint's rows are one upstream control step each (an EE or joint delta, the next waypoint
    of a trajectory), and ``exec_horizon`` / a video window's stride count env steps, so at another rate
    every chunk executes at the wrong speed, silently. ``subject`` names the client and setup
    (``"PiPolicy.policy_setup='droid'"``) and ``source`` where upstream sets the rate. ``timing`` is the
    ``(sim_dt as typed, decimation)`` the fix suggests, with ``timing_note`` appended (e.g. the
    ``sim_substeps`` a Robotiq 2F85 needs); ``None`` derives one from the env's ``sim_dt``. ``wrong_fix`` replaces
    the closing "do not rescale or resample the actions" sentence for a client with a more plausible wrong fix.
    """
    env_dt = float(env.dt)
    period = 1.0 / control_hz
    if math.isclose(env_dt, period, rel_tol=1e-6):
        return
    speed = f"{period / env_dt:.2f}x too fast" if env_dt < period else f"{env_dt / period:.2f}x too slow"
    if timing is None:
        decimation = max(1, round(period / env.sim_dt))
        exact = math.isclose(env.sim_dt * decimation, period, rel_tol=1e-6)
        timing = (f"{env.sim_dt!r}" if exact else f"1/{control_hz * decimation:g}", decimation)
    sim_dt, decimation = timing
    if wrong_fix is None:
        wrong_fix = (
            f"Do not rescale or resample the actions instead: the checkpoint's chunk is a trajectory at "
            f"{control_hz:g} Hz, and a faster env would also re-query the server that much more often."
        )
    raise ValueError(
        f"{subject} executes one action row per {period:.6f} s ({control_hz:g} Hz) control step, as {source}, but "
        f"the env steps every env.dt={env_dt:.6f} s (sim_dt * decimation), which would run each chunk {speed}. Fix: "
        f"build the env with sim_dt * decimation = 1/{control_hz:g} s, e.g. EnvOptions(sim_dt={sim_dt}, "
        f"decimation={decimation}){timing_note}. {wrong_fix}"
    )

When the env is built (it always is before a policy is constructed in the drivers), the two are compared so a mismatch is reported at setup time rather than silently ignored. Envs without an action manager (unit tests) skip.

    Every field of :data:GRIPPER_DECISION_FIELDS is compared: one the caller does not pass in expected must be at the controller's default, because hysteresis, a hold, a sticky latch or continuous mode each replace the plain threshold rule the caller relies on.

    Clients forward the server's raw gripper scalar, so any other gripper term (e.g. a task config's own BinaryJointController) would silently misread it: a missing term, a term of another type, or an expected field the term does not have all raise.

    def check_env_gripper_term(env, term_name: str, **expected) -> None:
    """Fail fast when the env's built gripper term disagrees with settings a policy also carries.

    Some client policies expose gripper knobs (thresholds, hold, decode mode) that the env's
    :class:`GripperDecisionController` also carries. When the env is built (it always is before a
    policy is constructed in the drivers), the two are compared so a mismatch is reported at
    setup time rather than silently ignored. Envs without an action manager (unit tests) skip.

    Every field of :data:`GRIPPER_DECISION_FIELDS` is compared: one the caller does not pass in
    ``expected`` must be at the controller's default, because hysteresis, a hold, a sticky latch or
    continuous mode each replace the plain threshold rule the caller relies on.

    Clients forward the server's raw gripper scalar, so any other gripper term (e.g. a task
    config's own ``BinaryJointController``) would silently misread it: a missing term, a term of
    another type, or an expected field the term does not have all raise.
    """
    from eden.managers.terms.actions.binary_actions import GripperDecisionController

    manager = getattr(env, "action_manager", None)
    if manager is None:
        return
    term = manager.terms.get(term_name)
    if term is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The env has no action term {term_name!r}; available: {sorted(manager.terms)}. Build the env "
            "with the policy's action_options() so its GripperDecisionController receives the gripper command."
        )
    if not isinstance(term, GripperDecisionController):
        raise TypeError(
            f"Action term {term_name!r} is a {type(term).__name__}, but this policy forwards the server's raw "
            "gripper scalar and needs a GripperDecisionController to interpret it. Build the env's gripper "
            "term from the policy's action_options()."
        )
    unknown = sorted(name for name in expected if not hasattr(term, name))
    if unknown:
        raise AttributeError(f"Gripper term {term_name!r} has no field(s) {unknown} to check against the policy.")
    undeclared = {
        name: getattr(GripperDecisionController, name) for name in GRIPPER_DECISION_FIELDS if name not in expected
    }
    mismatched = {
        name: (getattr(term, name), value)
        for name, value in {**expected, **undeclared}.items()
        if getattr(term, name) != value
    }
    if mismatched:
        details = ", ".join(
            f"{k}: env term has {a!r}, policy {'has' if k in expected else 'does not use it (default)'} {b!r}"
            for k, (a, b) in mismatched.items()
        )
        raise ValueError(
            f"Gripper term {term_name!r} was configured differently from the policy ({details}). "
            "The decision now lives in the env's GripperDecisionController: build the env's gripper term from "
            "the policy's action_options(), not from another client's or a task's own gripper term."
        )
